text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — our A/B of the new kernel selector vs legacy shows a 12-18% p99 latency regression under the replay harness but NOT under synthetic traffic. I think arrival patterns + KV-cache behavior are interacting badly.

Maria: interesting. do you have a short repro or a perf trace?

Alex: posting traces. baseline (legacy kernel): p50=48ms p95=160ms p99=320ms. new-selector: p50=50ms p95=170ms p99=375ms under replay. under synthetic constant-rate load new-selector p99 ~325ms (same as baseline).

Devon: that delta smells like batching heuristics. replay has bursty inter-arrival times which cause different batch composition & kernel pick. could also be KV cache thrash if request prefixes vary.

Sam: +1. specifically: if batches are smaller because arrivals are bursty then the selector might prefer a different GEMM kernel optimized for small B that has worse latency for our sequence length.

Maria: can you share the trace snippet where kernel choice changes?

Alex: here — trimmed trace: ```
kernel_select: model=redwood-base, seq=1024, batch=3 -> kernel=B_pack16
kernel_select: model=redwood-base, seq=1024, batch=8 -> kernel=B_pack32
kv_cache: hit_rate=0.72 -> drops to 0.58 during replay burst
batching: observed continuous_binning enabled -> batches split across slots
```

Devon: that kv hit drop is suspicious. If kv cache eviction occurs during a burst we pay serialization/memcopy + cold KV reads which inflates tail. Is the cache pinned per-model or per-worker?

Alex: per-worker with LRU eviction (default). In the replay we replay many user sessions with slightly different prefixes which defeats prefix-KV merging.

perf-bot: ran quick synthetic with poisson arrivals (lambda=60 rps) and replay harness (preserve arrival deltas). summary attached: synthetic p99=330ms, replay p99=375ms. KV hit delta ~14%.

Sam: ok — next steps: 1) force kernel to legacy one to isolate whether selector is root cause, 2) run replay with prefix-normalized traffic to isolate kv effect, 3) run dedicated pool with pre-warmed cache to test cold-start vs eviction.

Devon: to force kernel locally set env: ```export REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=legacy_gemm```. I can add a perf flag to the harness to iterate kernel options.

Maria: also add a synthetic test that reproduces the replay inter-arrival distribution (use empirical inter-arrival times). apples-to-apples means same arrival pattern + same input diversity.

Alex: agreed. I ran one quick experiment forcing kernel: new-selector + forced_legacy -> p99 back to 328ms (close to baseline). so selector is a major contributor. but KV hit still lower in replay, so both matter.

Sam: good find. what about autoscale / burst credits? do we see any scale-up delays that expose more cold cache windows?

Alex: yes — during a sustained replay surge we consumed burst credits on the shared hosted pool and some requests got routed to dedicated cold nodes. scale-up time measured ~24s to add a new worker (we hit target queue depth), which is enough to allow eviction churn.

Devon: dedicated pools should help. run dedicated-pool replay test with warmup stage (60s) and then surge. Compare p99 and KV hit. If dedicated with warmup eliminates regression then routing + scale-up is another axis.

perf-bot: queued jobs: 1) replay-forced-kernel, 2) replay-prefix-normalized, 3) dedicated-warmup-surge. ETA ~2h for full runs.

Maria: once perf-bot gives numbers, we should: a) consider kernel-hinting (allow forcing on per-route basis for now), b) adjust batching heuristics to prefer slightly larger batches when sequence length>512 even if latency SLO permits, c) evaluate prefix canonicalization / request coalescing to improve KV hit.

Alex: also filing a short regression PR to gate the new selector behind a feature flag until we have tuning. I'll add the traces & perf numbers.

Sam: +1 to feature flag. also add a small experiment: reduce LRU aggressiveness (bigger cache) for the replay workload to see hit-rate sensitivity.

Devon: I'll prototype a kernel-selection fallback: if p95 or p99 increases by >10% for route in 10m window, auto-fallback to previous kernel and mark route for manual review. That should reduce customer impact while we tune.

Alex: thanks team. action items in thread: Devon->kernel fallback prototype, Maria->arrival-pattern synthetic harness, Sam->dedicated-warmup test & cache config sweep, Alex->PR + traces + gating flag. perf-bot will post results. :thumbsup:
